newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAIDERS FIRE HEAD COACH MIKE WHITE ON CHRISTMAS EVE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAIDERS FIRE HEAD COACH MIKE WHITE ON CHRISTMAS EVE.

text.p: Oakland Raiders owner Al Davis played Scrooge on Tuesday, firing head coach Mike White on Christmas Eve following a disappointing season.
White, who became Oakland's 10th head coach in February of 1995, was unable to take his team into the playoffs in two seasons with Oakland.
He guided the Raiders to a 7-9 record this season after an 8-8 campaign in 1995.
The Raiders won eight of their first 10 games under White, but the team's six-game losing streak to end the 1995 season cost them a playoff berth.

The Raiders were terribly inconsistent this season, getting off to a slow 1-4 start. They kept their slim 1996 playoff hopes alive with a modest late-season three-game winning streak that brought their record up to 7-7. But a loss to Denver on December 15 ended their post-season chances and Oakland finished with a loss to Seattle.
The Raiders lost seven games by a touchdown or less, including a pair of consecutive overtime defeats.
White served as quarterbacks coach for the Raiders from 1990-92 and was offensive line coach the following two seasons before taking over the top spot.
The 60-year-old White is the fifth National Football League head coach to be relieved of his job in the closing days of the 1996 regular season.

On Monday, the New York Giants fired Dan Reeves and the Atlanta Falcons let June Jones go. One day earlier, the St Louis Rams gave Rich Brooks his walking papers. New York Jets coach Rich Kotite stepped down before the axe could fall after guiding his team to a miserable franchise-worst 1-15 record.
